verdict.rationale: pnpm's docs explicitly position it as a drop-in replacement for npm that can be pointed at any existing project without migration. It mirrors familiar verbs (`pnpm i`, `pnpm update`, `pnpm audit --fix`, `pnpm sbom` alongside `npm sbom`), and a `hoisted` nodeLinker recreates the npm/Yarn Classic node_modules layout. Migrators report success, using `--shamefully-hoist` for compatibility. One user found the commands 'a little fussier' than Yarn's, and behaviors like peer-dependency installation differ from npm 7+, so the parity is not seamless. missing for 10: a documented command-by-command parity map with npm/Yarn, independent hands-on confirmation that the CLI conventions match the incumbent, and resolution of differing defaults (peer deps, strict layout).
